messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Your doctor will check whether the medicine is still working as intended.
Insulin and oral diabetes medicines.
Your diabetes medicine dose may need adjusting.
Corticosteroids and ACTH.
These increase the loss of salts from the body.
The loss of salts is particularly potassium.
This effect occurs when taken with hydrochlorothiazide.
Digoxin and other digitalis medicines.
Low potassium caused by hydrochlorothiazide can make the heart more sensitive to the toxic effects of digitalis.
These toxic effects include irregular heart rhythms.
Other blood pressure medicines.
The effects add together.
This may be intended.
However, it can also lower blood pressure more than expected.
Alcohol, barbiturates and opioid pain medicines.
Alcohol, barbiturates and opioid pain medicines can make the drop in blood pressure on standing worse.
This can cause dizziness or fainting.
Muscle relaxants used during surgery (nondepolarizing muscle relaxants such as tubocurarine).
You may respond more strongly to Muscle relaxants.
Tell your surgeon and anesthetist that you take hydrochlorothiazide.
Triples: [["hydrochlorothiazide", "interacts with", "insulin"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "interacts with", "oral diabetes medicines"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "interacts with", "corticosteroids"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "interacts with", "ACTH"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "causes", "loss of salts"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "causes", "loss of potassium"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "has effect when taken with", "digoxin"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "has effect when taken with", "other digitalis medicines"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "causes", "low potassium"], ["low potassium", "increases sensitivity to", "digitalis"], ["digitalis", "has toxic effect", "irregular heart rhythms"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "interacts with", "other blood pressure medicines"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "has additive effect with", "other blood pressure medicines"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "has effect when taken with", "alcohol"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "has effect when taken with", "barbiturates"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "has effect when taken with", "opioid pain medicines"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "increases effect of", "alcohol"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "increases effect of", "barbiturates"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "increases effect of", "opioid pain medicines"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "causes", "drop in blood pressure on standing"], ["drop in blood pressure on standing", "can cause", "dizziness"], ["drop in blood pressure on standing", "can cause", "fainting"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "interacts with", "muscle relaxants"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "increases effect of", "muscle relaxants"], ["hydrochlorothiazide", "has administration instruction", "tell your surgeon and anesthetist that you take hydrochlorothiazide"]]
Relations: ["can cause", "causes", "has additive effect with", "has administration instruction", "has effect when taken with", "has toxic effect", "increases effect of", "increases sensitivity to", "interacts with"]
Answer:

completion:
can cause: The subject condition or event may lead to the outcome or symptom specified by the object entity.  
causes: The subject drug or condition directly results in the effect or outcome specified by the object entity.  
has additive effect with: The subject drug, when taken with the object drug, may produce combined or enhanced effects.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the specific medical instruction or action specified by the object entity.  
has effect when taken with: The subject drug may have a specific effect or interaction when taken in combination with the object drug or substance.  
has toxic effect: The subject drug or substance can produce harmful or dangerous effects specified by the object entity.  
increases effect of: The subject drug enhances or intensifies the effect of the object drug or substance.  
increases sensitivity to: The subject condition or drug makes the object drug or substance more potent or dangerous.  
interacts with: The subject drug may have a pharmacological interaction or combined effect when taken with the object drug or substance.
